body:
Background sync itself already exists: `SyncScheduler.schedulePeriodic()`
enqueues a network-constrained WorkManager periodic request every 15
minutes (`SyncWorker` -> `SyncEngine.syncNow()`), independent of whether
the app is foregrounded — that's true background sync today, not new
scope here. The actual net-new work is: when a background (or foreground)
sync pulls a change that was NOT made by the current user, post a local
Android notification ("3 items changed in Groceries — tap to view").

Depends on T-64 (item last-touched-by): detecting "changed by someone
else" must compare against the ACCOUNT that made the change, not the
per-field `_by` device_id. Device-level comparison would misfire
constantly for any user with 2+ devices on the same account (phone +
tablet is a realistic self-hosting scenario) — every sync of their OWN
second device would look like "a collaborator changed this." Don't build
this on device_id; wait for T-64's `last_touched_by_account_id`.

Scope, once T-64 is available:
- `SyncEngine.syncNow()` (or `SyncWorker` around it) needs to know, per
  pulled item/list, whether `last_touched_by_account_id` differs from the
  current account — and only for rows that actually changed in this sync
  pass (not just "not mine", since most rows on every pull weren't
  authored by you and haven't changed either).
- Notification permission: `POST_NOTIFICATIONS` runtime permission on API
  33+ (request it somewhere sensible — Settings, or on first detected
  need — not a cold-start prompt).
- One `NotificationChannel`, tap-to-open the affected list (or overview if
  multiple lists changed in one sync pass).
- Batch per sync run, not per changed row — a sync that pulls 12 changed
  items across 2 lists is one or two notifications, not twelve.
- A sync that finds no changes from other accounts stays completely
  silent (the common case, every 15 minutes, for a solo list).

Open for whoever implements: per-list mute/Settings toggle for
notifications, and whether foreground syncs (app open) should also
notify or only background ones (arguably pointless to notify about
something already visible on screen).

Platform scope: Android only. Browser push notifications for the web
client would need a service worker + push subscription + a push-capable
server component — a different, much larger undertaking, explicitly out
of scope here.
title: Android: notify when a collaborator changes a shared list (background sync already exists)
